specs.scene: A florist's stainless steel workbench surface, crowded to all four edges with the physical debris of a working flower shop: buckets of cut stems, a spool of ribbon partly unwound, sheets of kraft paper, a stack of paper order tickets, a handwritten delivery docket, floral foam blocks, pruning shears, a roll of florist tape, and a small stack of invoice slips. One hand grips shears mid-cut on a stem, the other pins an order ticket to a wrapped bouquet. Small bare patches of the steel surface remain visible between the clustered objects. All surfaces are positively blank, no readable text or branding on any item.
specs.source_quote: I tell them it's a dial tone. You never think about it until it stops

recognisable.why: Florist-shop objects (stems, ribbon, shears) read as a familiar trade at a glance, though the shop itself has no household name.

legibility.why: The clustered items read as one gestalt mass, a busy workbench, rather than several separate elements the viewer must resolve.

curiosity.why: The overlay states an unresolved verdict, implying a failure the viewer cannot see or predict.

subject.why: Hands mid-action anchor the frame, though a full person is not shown.

credible.why: No figure is carried, which the rubric scores full.

stakes.why: Implies operational risk to the business if the invisible system fails, though it is not spelled out.

reexpress.why: The overlay supplies the consequence of failure, which none of the title options state.
